input.plan:
# CLIENT workflow and clone manifests

## What is true today

`mode` is read once in [`app/routes/shared.py`](app/routes/shared.py) (`CLIENT` unless config says `SERVER`). It is not passed to JavaScript.

| Intended CLIENT behavior | Actual code |
|---|---|
| Play local only | Local HTML5 is the default because `stream_mode` is `local`, on both modes. Cast still works if someone connects a device. |
| Hide Chromecast | Bottom transport bar is SERVER-only in [`app/templates/index.html`](app/templates/index.html). Cast icon, menu, discovery thread, and [`app/routes/cast_routes.py`](app/routes/cast_routes.py) stay active on CLIENT. |
| Clone from the server on scan when the server is reachable | Scan in CLIENT calls [`content_transfer.query_server()`](app/utils/content_transfer.py) after the first disk pass ([`backend_handler.py`](app/utils/backend_handler.py)). It always targets configured `server_url`, pulls every DB-missing MP4 (plus images), and has no per-client record. A failed pull still reports “Scan complete (synced from server)” because the return value is ignored. |

There is no client id, registry, or manifest. Handshake tokens are shared secrets, not device identity.

Confirmed product rules for the new sync:

- With no saved manifest, a CLIENT scan downloads nothing (it may still register and upload its catalog if the server answers).
- Skip the pull unless `server_url` answers. Ethernet to that URL counts; do not check a Wi-Fi interface.

## CLIENT: local playback, no cast

- In [`app/templates/top_navbar.html`](app/templates/top_navbar.html), render the cast chip and `#chromecast_menu` only when `system_mode == "SERVER"`.
- In [`app/static/js/app_main.js`](app/static/js/app_main.js), call `getChromecastList` only when that menu exists.
- Do not start `ChromecastHandler` when mode is CLIENT ([`BackEndHandler.get_chromecast`](app/utils/backend_handler.py)). Read mode inside the backend (same config check as `shared.py`) so `shared` → `backend_handler` does not gain a cycle.
- Cast routes return 404 in CLIENT mode. `play_media` keeps resolving `local_play_url` and does not call cast when the handler is absent.
- Local config and [`tests/pytest_mocks.py`](tests/pytest_mocks.py) stay `mode: SERVER`, so existing cast tests keep a handler.

## Sync: reachability, identity, manifest-scoped pull

Extend the CLIENT scan path; do not add a second sync trigger.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant Server
    Client->>Server: POST /server_connect client_id plus secret
    alt Unreachable
        Server-->>Client: timeout
        Note over Client: Local scan only
    else Reachable
        Server-->>Client: token plus empty or saved manifest
        Client->>Server: POST inventory of local content_src
        Client->>Client: Delete manifest.remove under media roots
        Client->>Server: Download manifest.clone files only
    end
```

- **Identity:** `client_name` in `app/config.json` if set, otherwise `socket.gethostname()`, sanitized to a filename (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]`).
- **Reachability:** existing `server_request` timeout. Connect failure returns `{status: "skipped"}`. [`start_scan_media_directories`](app/utils/backend_handler.py) stores that message on `last_scan_result` (local scan still finishes; second pass still runs so deletions/new files are cataloged when a sync did run).
- **No manifest / empty `clone`:** register the client, store inventory, download zero files. This replaces “pull every missing MP4”.
- **Downloads:** only `clone` entries, by `content_src` (lookup on the server; ids differ per database). Pull cover images only for those entries. Keep the 2GB cap and MD5 check.
- **Removals:** `remove` entries are deleted on the client only when the resolved path is under a configured media root, then dropped from the manifest’s pending remove list after a successful delete report. A path in both lists is a removal (the page will not save that overlap). Order on the client: delete, then download.

Manifest directory: `var/clone_manifests/<client_id>.json` (gitignored). One current file per client, not a new SQLite table and no `DBConnection.VERSION` bump.

```json
{
  "client_id": "living-room-pi",
  "display_name": "Living Room Pi",
  "last_seen": "2026-11-13T15:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-11-13T14:00:00Z",
  "inventory": [{"content_src": "movies/Title (2010).mp4"}],
  "clone": [{"content_src": "tv_shows/Show - s01e01.mp4"}],
  "remove": []
}
```

**Active** means `last_seen` within 15 minutes (a scan session). **Historical** means any older manifest file. No heartbeat thread.

## SERVER page (transfer-client layout)

New gear-menu item **Clone**, SERVER-only, same pattern as Editor (`get_media_content_types` adds the URL; [`setNavbarLinks`](app/static/js/app_main.js) unhides it).

New template [`app/templates/clone.html`](app/templates/clone.html) plus [`app/static/js/clone.js`](app/static/js/clone.js) (page-local script, not part of the global load order). Bootstrap, no bundler. Layout matches a classic two-pane transfer client:

- Header: client `<select>` grouped into Active and Historical, plus last seen and last manifest save time.
- Left pane: this server’s catalog (`content_src`, title), filter box, multi-select.
- Right pane: that client’s last reported inventory (stale if offline; show the timestamp).
- Actions: **Add to clone**, **Remove from client** (frees space on the next sync), **Save manifest**.

Endpoints (new `APIEndpoints` in [`shared.py`](app/routes/shared.py), handlers in [`transfer_routes.py`](app/routes/transfer_routes.py) or a small `clone_routes.py` imported from [`app/routes/__init__.py`](app/routes/__init__.py)):

- `GET /clone` — page, SERVER only
- `GET /clone/clients` — active and historical list
- `GET /clone/catalog` — server media rows
- `GET /clone/clients/<id>` — manifest + inventory
- `POST /clone/clients/<id>` — replace `clone` and `remove` (JSON). UI-only; handshake is not required on loopback LAN, matching the rest of the app (no Flask auth).

Client-facing additions stay on the existing handshake:

- `POST /server_connect` accepts `client_id` / `display_name`, upserts the file, returns the manifest
- `POST /client_inventory` stores `inventory` and refreshes `last_seen`

`request_content` gains a `content_src` lookup so the client can fetch a manifest entry without a local id. Paths still have to sit under media roots.

## Tests and docs

Unit tests in [`tests/test_content_transfer_unit.py`](tests/test_content_transfer_unit.py) (temp manifest dir, mocked HTTP):

- Unreachable `server_url` → skipped, no download
- Connect with inventory and an empty manifest → zero downloads, file created
- Manifest `clone` of one `content_src` → only that file requested
- `remove` deletes an in-root file and refuses a path outside media roots
- CLIENT cast route / handler start stays off when mode is patched to CLIENT

README: CLIENT plays local and does not cast; scan pulls only the saved manifest when `server_url` answers; Clone page and `var/clone_manifests/` described. Mention backing up that directory the same way as `media_metadata.db` if the manifests matter.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/ -m "not integration" -q`
- SERVER: open `/clone`, select a client (or the empty state), save a one-title manifest, reload and confirm the selection stuck.
- CLIENT config (or a rendered `index.html` with `system_mode=CLIENT`): no cast control in the top nav; gear menu has no Clone link.

todos.content: Hide Chromecast UI and skip ChromecastHandler/cast routes when mode is CLIENT; keep play local
Per-client JSON manifests, inventory on connect, reachability skip, clone-only download and in-root delete
SERVER /clone dual-pane page: active/historical clients, catalog, save clone and remove lists
Unit tests for sync/manifest/cast gate; README note; browser check of /clone and CLIENT nav

<user_query>
This stack will run on a RPi 4, suggest ideal lightweight OS to support webapp running in kiosk mode and static auto mounting usb disks
</user_query>
The app already assumes a small Linux service layout. I’ll check how it starts and how disks are expected to mount so the OS suggestion matches that.

Use **Raspberry Pi OS Lite 64-bit** (the current Debian image). It is the smallest OS that already matches this repo: `apt`, systemd, and the packages in `setup.sh` (`python3-venv`, `ffmpeg`, `npm`, `sqlite3`). The desktop image spends RAM on a session you would only use to fullscreen one page.

Skip Alpine (breaks `setup.sh` and Python wheels) and Ubuntu (extra weight, weaker Pi integration). DietPi is smaller, but its disk automount is label-based and drifts from the fixed paths in `app/config.json`. Chromium, not the base OS, is what uses the memory. A 4 GB Pi 4 is the comfortable size; 2 GB is tight once the kiosk is open.

## Kiosk

Lite has no desktop. Boot to an autologin user and run one full-screen browser against the local app:

- Flask stays the existing production unit, [`system_services/chromecast_controller.service`](system_services/chromecast_controller.service), on port 5000.
- Chromium kiosk: `cage -s -- chromium --kiosk --noerrdialogs http://127.0.0.1:5000`
- `cage` is a single-app Wayland compositor. Do not install the Raspberry Pi desktop just to get a browser.
- Run that as a user service after `network-online.target` and the Flask service, not as root.
- Turn off console blanking so the player does not sleep.

On a CLIENT box, set `content_url` to `http://127.0.0.1:8000/`. Playback then does not depend on the LAN address changing.

## USB disks at fixed paths

“Static auto mount” here means **fstab by filesystem UUID**, not a desktop automounter that mounts whatever label appears under `/media/<user>/`.

1. `blkid` the disk once.
2. Mount it at a path you will put in `content_src`, for example `/media/library`.
3. Use `nofail` and a short device timeout so boot still finishes when the disk is unplugged:

```fstab
UUID=xxxx-xxxx  /media/library  ext4  nofail,x-systemd.device-timeout=10,x-systemd.automount  0  2
```

`x-systemd.automount` mounts on first access and again if the disk is plugged in later. Prefer ext4. NTFS/exFAT needs extra packages and does not give you normal Unix owners for the scan and http-server user.

Point [`system_services/media_drive_as_webpage.service`](system_services/media_drive_as_webpage.service) at that same directory and start it only after the mount (`RequiresMountsFor=/media/library`). The unit today starts `http-server` with no mount dependency, so it can come up on an empty directory.

Power the disk from a powered hub. A Pi 4’s USB budget is a common reason a mount works once and then disappears. Keep the OS and SQLite on the SD card; keep the library on the USB disk.

<timestamp>Friday, Nov 13, 2026, 11:01 AM (UTC-5)</timestamp>
<user_query>
The headless Raspberry Pi OS Lite 64-bit will be able to present the kiosked browser?
</user_query>

Yes. Lite still drives the HDMI port. It only omits the desktop, so you add a fullscreen browser and a tiny display program instead of the full Raspberry Pi desktop.

“Headless” here means it boots to a text console. The Pi 4’s display hardware is still there. With a monitor on HDMI, a user autologin on tty1 can start `cage` and Chromium; that pair takes the screen and shows `http://127.0.0.1:5000` with no taskbar and no desktop session. Those packages are not on the Lite image until you install them.

A Pi with no monitor attached has nowhere to show that window. SSH still works, and Flask still serves the page, but the kiosk itself needs the HDMI display.

input.overview: Add a root bash script that prepares a Raspberry Pi OS Lite client: kiosk Chromium against the existing Flask service, console blanking off, and one static USB automount plus http-server unit per disk.
input.plan:
# Client kiosk and USB setup script

Add [`setup_client.sh`](setup_client.sh) at the repo root. Run it as root from a checkout that already has `.venv` (`sudo ./setup.sh` creates that). The script installs units under `/etc/systemd/system` and does not `sed -i` the repo templates (unlike [`setup.sh`](setup.sh), which rewrites `INSTALL_USER` in place).

## Apt packages

`chromium`, `cage`, `npm`, `exfatprogs`, `ntfs-3g`. Then `npm install -g http-server` when `http-server` is not on `PATH`. Add the invoking user (`SUDO_USER`) to `video`, `render`, and `input` so `cage` can open HDMI.

Exit early if `.venv` is missing, with a message to run `sudo ./setup.sh` first. [`start_server`](start_server) refuses to boot Flask without it.

## Services

Install the existing Flask unit by copying [`system_services/chromecast_controller.service`](system_services/chromecast_controller.service) through `sed` into `/etc/systemd/system`, substituting `INSTALL_USER` and `INSTALL_DIR` (the repo root). Enable it. Production `start_server` listens on port 5000.

Add a repo template [`system_services/chromium_kiosk.service`](system_services/chromium_kiosk.service) and install it the same way:

- `After=` / `Wants=chromecast_controller.service`
- `User=INSTALL_USER`
- `ExecStart=/usr/bin/cage -s -- /usr/bin/chromium --kiosk --noerrdialogs --disable-infobars --check-for-update-interval=31536000 http://127.0.0.1:5000`
- `Restart=always`, `WantedBy=multi-user.target`

## Console blanking

If `/boot/firmware/cmdline.txt` exists, otherwise `/boot/cmdline.txt`, append `consoleblank=0` when that token is absent. Blanking stays off across reboot. The script prints that a reboot is required for the kernel flag.

## USB automount

For each partition from `lsblk -rno NAME,TRAN,FSTYPE,UUID,LABEL` whose parent disk has `TRAN=usb`, has a `UUID` and an `FSTYPE` of `ext4`, `vfat`, `exfat`, or `ntfs`, and is not the root filesystem:

- Mount point `/media/usb/<sanitized-label-or-uuid>`
- Skip when that UUID is already in `/etc/fstab`
- Append a marked line, `nofail,x-systemd.device-timeout=10,x-systemd.automount`
- `vfat` / `exfat` / `ntfs` also get `uid=` / `gid=` of `SUDO_USER`
- `mkdir` the mount point and `systemctl daemon-reload` so the automount unit is active

No USB partitions is a warning, not a failure. The kiosk still installs.

## http-server per disk

For each mount point just ensured, write `/etc/systemd/system/media_drive_<n>.service` from [`system_services/media_drive_as_webpage.service`](system_services/media_drive_as_webpage.service):

- `WorkingDirectory=` that mount point
- `ExecStart=http-server -p <port>` with ports `8000`, `8001`, … in lsblk order
- `RequiresMountsFor=` the mount point
- `User=` the install user

Enable those units. Update [`app/config.json`](app/config.json) with Python (no new package): `mode` = `CLIENT`, and `media_folders` to one entry per mount (`content_src` = mount path, `content_url` = `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/`). The kiosk only plays locally, so the loopback URL stays valid when DHCP changes.

## Docs and check

One short README subsection: `sudo ./setup_client.sh` from the repo, then reboot. Verify with `bash -n setup_client.sh`. Live HDMI, USB, and systemd cannot be checked in this environment.

todos.content: Add setup_client.sh: apt, Flask unit, kiosk unit, consoleblank=0, USB fstab automounts, per-disk http-server units, config.json CLIENT media_folders
Add system_services/chromium_kiosk.service template and a short README setup note; bash -n the script

## Display stays on

The Pi must not blank the console, power down HDMI, or suspend.

- Append `consoleblank=0` to `/boot/firmware/cmdline.txt`, or `/boot/cmdline.txt` if that is the file present, when the token is absent.
- In `/boot/firmware/config.txt` (else `/boot/config.txt`), set `hdmi_force_hotplug=1` so the HDMI port stays driven when the display drops hotplug.
- In `/etc/systemd/logind.conf`, set `IdleAction=ignore` (replace an existing `IdleAction=` line, or add one under `[Login]`).
- Mask `sleep.target`, `suspend.target`, `hibernate.target`, and `hybrid-sleep.target` so logind cannot suspend the board.
- Print that a reboot is required before the kernel and config.txt flags apply.

`cage` has no idle blanker. These settings cover the console, HDMI hotplug, and systemd sleep, which are what turn the panel off on Pi OS Lite.

## Client OS cleanup

Ethernet only. The script leaves NetworkManager and SSH in place so a cable can still reach `server_url` and an admin shell.

- Append `dtoverlay=disable-wifi` and `dtoverlay=disable-bt` to `config.txt` when those lines are absent. That cuts the radios in firmware, including after reboot, which `rfkill` alone does not.
- `systemctl disable --now` these units when they exist: `bluetooth`, `hciuart`, `wpa_supplicant`. Do not fail if a unit is missing.
- Do not install a desktop, cups, or ModemManager. The apt list stays the kiosk and filesystem packages already named.

The setup script still leaves a few choices open. These are the ones that change what it should do.

❓ **Q1** — **How the client finds the server:** Wi-Fi is off, and the script never writes `server_url`. Local playback uses `127.0.0.1`, so the Pi can play files with no LAN address, but a scan cannot clone until `server_url` points at the home server. Should the script require `SERVER_URL=http://192.168.x.x:5000` and write that into `app/config.json`, or leave `server_url` for you to edit by hand?

➡️ Require `SERVER_URL` and write it. A client image that boots with an empty `server_url` looks finished and never syncs.

---

❓ **Q2** — **SSH:** The script keeps SSH and NetworkManager so you can still administer the Pi over the Ethernet cable. The kiosk owns the HDMI screen, and the radios are disabled, so a bad boot is hard to recover without a shell.

➡️ Keep SSH enabled.

---

❓ **Q3** — **Kiosk process:** `cage` can run as a system service that conflicts with `getty@tty1`, which is what the plan does. The other model is console autologin and a user service, which is more reliable when the system unit cannot open `/dev/dri`.

➡️ System service, conflicting with `getty@tty1`, as you asked. Switch to autologin only if that fails on the Pi.

---

❓ **Q4** — **Running the script again:** A disk that is unplugged during a later run is still supposed to automount when it returns. If the script rebuilds `media_folders` from only the disks present right now, an unplugged library disappears from the catalog config.

➡️ Only add fstab lines and `media_folders` entries. Leave existing managed USB entries in place when the disk is absent.
